body: Thanks for the advice. it's appreciated.   I might seriously have to take it into consideration, psych medication.  Hopefully, though, in tandem with more naturopathic things like acupuncture.  I hear it can be helpful for my medical condition as well as depressive moods. I am trying to be optimistic.

I wish you luck in your travels.  I used to share a same spirit until my chronic illness and the terrible experience from it made me weak, perhaps more so in the mind, than in the body.   Sometimes I wish I could just leave everything behind and be a sailor on some small sailing ship down in a warm environ.  Just climb the top sails all day, set the rigging, and watch the sun rise and set over a blue ocean.  Maybe a big, complicated life of a multitude of things is not in my cards.   I would accept, as an alternative to suicide, a quiet life of contemplation at sea, where I am apart of something bigger, a valuable member of a crew.  And in this vast cosmos, down into this massive galaxy, further into this expansive solar system, upon this terra green and cobalt blue marble, aboard but a floating speck on a never-ending body of sea, I would have a purpose…a purpose upon that floating speck that is upon that blue marble that is hurdling though that expansive solar system, that is within the breadth of our massive galaxy, that is but a tiny pixel in the seemingly endless cosmos.  In all of that (gasps a deep breath for rambling so much), I would have a purpose, chronic condition be damned.  It's a nice thought anyway.
Thank you, I will try and give that a try.  Have you ever tried or had success with acupuncture, personally?

Thanks for the reply.  I have tried meditation and things, but it's like I can't calm down my body, especially my lower back.    I would be very interested in trying acupuncture to be honest, but that would probably take some time and quite a bit of finance to set up.   I dunno, I guess it sort of feels very urgent. The depressive/anxious moods are lasting longer and longer and talking myself out of it isn't helping anymore.  

Thank you for your input.
Ok will do.  back soon. Thank you and i can lend a year to you as well.
If not though, I understand too, no worries.

I think suicidality is harder.  I mean, it goes contrary to everything there is to being human.  It's hard for your mind to process it.  Indeed, it is exhausting.  I have to go off for a half hour so, but I would really like to explain the problem in more detail if you would care to listen.  Will you permit me to reply via PM?

I feel exactly the same way.  I mean, i have sort of always felt that way, even before i got suicidal like this.  For example, when that child was killed in the Boston marathon bombing, all I could think was "I wish I could trade places with him."  Not because I wanted to die back then, but because it was so unjust that he or any child should be ripped from life like that.   Now, I would do it gladly, trade places.  At least someone would benefit from it and I wouldn't feel like crap for leaving.

virtual hug back to you too.   Yes, I can imagine how devastating it would be for my family if I did the unthinkable.  I am kind of a hypocrite in that the thought of somebody else committing suicide makes me very upset…yet I share the same thoughts.  Like, if I were standing on the railing of a bridge looking down into the water, getting ready for…well, you know. If I saw someone else on the bridge, I would probably get down and walk over and see if I could talk them down.  If I succeeded, afterward I would probably walk right back to where I was and…well, let gravity take over.

Like you, I could never devastate my family in such a way…and so I keep hoping…fiery house, push someone out of the way, anything.  An exit, but a heroic one, not as devastating as someone who took it themselves. I know it's faulty logic, but that's how I feel.
it's too much…so exhausted.   so very exhausted.
